newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPALS -- Prices up 1/8 to 1/4 point.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPALS -- Prices up 1/8 to 1/4 point.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds rose 1/8 to 1/4 point in early trade after a string of U.S. economic reports including the July Consumer Price Index came in largely as expected.

"I think the majority is that we were a little oversold, and we are getting a little bit of a bounce here," one trader said. "I think there was a lot of fear that inflation numbers were going to come in a little higher than expected, and they did not."
CPI matched economists' expectations, rising 0.2 percent overall as well as in the core rate. Weekly jobless claims rose to 316,000 from a revised 304,000. Expectations called for a rise to 317,000.

Later, the Federal Reserve Board reported that July industrial production rose 0.2 percent, matching economists' expectations. Capacity utilization fell to 83.1 percent from the previous report's 83.3 percent level. Economists called for a 83.5 percent reading.

In the government market, the benchmark 30-year bond was up 13/32 at 97-5/32 to yield 6.59 percent. In debt futures, the September municipal contract was up 14/32 at 119-16/32. The September T-bond contract was up 16/32 at 113-11/32. The MOB spread was 198 ticks.

While muni cash prices were higher, trading volume was light, the trader said. Actively quoted bonds included Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority 5.0 percent bonds of March 2024. The bonds had a 5.53 percent net bid, versus Wednesday's closing net bid of 5.58 percent.
Thursday's municipal bond sales are expected to total $213 million in 18 offerings, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Seven negotiated offerings totalled $105 million are scheduled, with a $35 million Jefferson Parish, La., offering through John Nuveen & Co., Inc. topping the list.
On the competitive side, 11 sales totaling $108 million are scheduled. A $36 million Worcester, Mass., offering at 1100 EDT is the largest.
An additional five sales totaling $193 million remain on the possible calender, meaning underwriters have said they may price the issues Thursday depending on market conditions.
